converged_beliefs.content: Critical alerts must deliver within 500ms end-to-end from event ingestion to delivery confirmation. This 500ms threshold is clinician-tested and hospital pilots showed 40% faster response times. The 99.9th percentile latency must be ≤500ms, 99th percentile must be ≤350ms, and any single critical alert exceeding 750ms constitutes immediate test failure. Operational alerts trigger when critical alert latency exceeds 500ms.

Four urgency tiers are defined: Critical (pager + push, immediate delivery), High (push within 30s with expedited routing), Normal (push within 5min with best-effort delivery), Low (batched hourly summaries with batched processing).
Critical alerts require one-tap acknowledgment with automatic escalation if the recipient doesn't respond within 60 seconds.

All notifications must fit in 4KB or less to optimize for in-memory buffering without disk spillover and keep mobile delivery snappy. Exact 4KB threshold enforcement: 3.9KB must pass, 4.0KB must pass, 4.1KB must fail with HTTP 413 (Payload Too Large) response. Oversized payloads must be rejected in sub-millisecond time.

Automatic retry with exponential backoff: 3 maximum retry attempts to avoid alert spam when a phone is genuinely offline. Backoff intervals are 1s → 2s → 4s, capped at 30s maximum. Retries run independently per channel. Notifications are marked as permanently failed after 3 failed attempts. CONTRADICTION RESOLVED: QA Engineer specified 5 retry attempts with intervals 1s, 2s, 4s, 8s, 16s, but the specification owner (PM) and architect both specify 3 attempts as the correct requirement.
converged_beliefs.resolution_detail: QA Engineer (b49) specified 5 retry attempts, but PM (specification owner), Architect, Lead Developer, and Technical Writer all specify 3 attempts. The 5-source consensus (3 attempts) overrides the single dissenting test specification.

converged_beliefs.content: Ingestion nodes validate, enrich, and partition messages by priority level within 50ms, leaving 450ms for delivery and confirmation to meet the 500ms critical alert latency requirement. Critical path eliminates synchronous database writes and demands edge-processing capabilities.

The system enforces 100 notifications/second sustained rate per provider/delivery channel with 150/second burst capacity. Token bucket algorithm uses 500 tokens (not 100) providing 10 seconds of burst capacity with 10-second refill window. Rate limiting is implemented at the provider adapter layer.

24-hour delivery guarantee: any notification stuck longer than 24 hours moves to dead letter queue for manual review. DLQ uses time-series partitioned storage in DynamoDB with TTL disabled for DLQ partitions. DLQ entries persist indefinitely and are never auto-deleted. SECURITY GAP IDENTIFIED: The 24-hour DLQ retention before manual review creates a breach notification exposure and requires automated alerting for DLQ entries containing PHI within 1 hour of failure per Security Reviewer.

Searchable 7-year audit trail is required per HIPAA §164.530(j) for all notification events (delivery attempts, failures, acknowledgments). Uses append-only log architecture with PostgreSQL partitioning by month. Logs are immutable after creation. Estimated 500GB/year of audit data per region. CONTRADICTION RESOLVED: QA Engineer specified 5-year retention as acceptance threshold, but PM (specification owner), Architect, Security Reviewer, and Technical Writer all confirm 7 years per HIPAA §164.530(j) regulatory requirement.
converged_beliefs.resolution_detail: QA Engineer (b51) specified 5-year retention as acceptance threshold, but regulatory compliance requirements per HIPAA §164.530(j) mandate 7 years as confirmed by PM, Architect, Security Reviewer, Lead Developer, and Technical Writer. Regulatory requirement overrides test acceptance criteria.

converged_beliefs.content: Apache Kafka requires 3-node cluster minimum for event ingestion and routing with 12 partitions per region minimum to handle burst loads. Regional Kafka clusters configured with min.insync.replicas=2.

Each relay node maintains exactly 10,000 concurrent WebSocket connections using epoll/kqueue for I/O multiplexing (Node.js with Socket.io). Memory consumption must be <8GB per node at 10K connections with CPU utilization <70% and <2% connection drop rate. 4-6 relay instances planned per region providing 60K total connection capacity. Connection establishment time must remain <200ms during scalability testing.

High-priority consumers get 60% of processing capacity, normal gets 30%, low gets 10% to prevent priority inversion during load spikes. Critical priority notifications use dedicated Kafka partition with acks=1 (not all) to save approximately 50ms latency for sub-second delivery requirement.

Regional failover uses active-passive relay node pairs with 30s failure detection window + 60s standby promotion = 90s maximum client disruption window. Health checks run every 5 seconds via HTTP /health endpoints checking Kafka connectivity, downstream provider availability, and memory pressure. WebSocket clients implement exponential reconnection (2s → 4s → 8s) to handle failover scenarios.

AES-256 encryption for all stored patient data meets NIST standards and HIPAA §164.312(a)(2)(iv) addressable specifications. 90-day key rotation via AWS KMS aligns with industry best practices. Simulate 90-day rotation cycles with verification of zero downtime and seamless re-encryption.

WebSocket connections carrying PHI must enforce TLS 1.2 minimum with forward secrecy cipher suites (ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384 or equivalent) per HIPAA §164.312(e)(1) transmission security requirements. HashiCorp Vault serves as certificate authority with 24-hour certificate lifetimes.
Client API authentication uses JWT tokens with 15-minute expiration and automatic refresh token rotation. Tokens are verified at API gateway with 30-second clock skew tolerance.
Circuit breaker pattern configured to fail fast after 5 consecutive errors to prevent provider API instability cascade.

Horizontal scaling required when cluster-wide connections exceed 80% of total capacity. WebSocket connection limits are mitigated via horizontal scaling with autoscale triggered at 8,000 connections/node.
Critical alert latency exceeding 500ms triggers operational alert. Failed notification rate exceeding 5% triggers investigation.

SECURITY GAP IDENTIFIED: The specification completely omits multi-factor authentication (MFA) requirement for administrative access or privileged operations. Healthcare workforce members accessing PHI-containing notification systems must authenticate via MFA per institutional security baseline derived from HIPAA §164.312(d) requirements.

SECURITY GAP IDENTIFIED: The specification completely omits role-based access control (RBAC) requirements and permission models required by HIPAA §164.312(a)(1) and minimum necessary access principles required by §164.502(b).

Deploy synthetic load generators simulating 5,000 concurrent critical alerts across all delivery channels for latency validation. Sustained load test: 100 notifications/second per provider for 60 minutes. Burst test: 150/second for 10-second windows with 20-second recovery periods. Connection scalability: linear scale from 1,000 to 12,000 connections over 10 minutes. Stress test must push to 15,000 connections to identify failure boundaries.

pruned_beliefs.reason: Security Reviewer's dismissive characterization of failover timing as non-compliance-grade is opinion/tone without actionable technical detail. The failover timing itself is preserved in cb13.
Project timeline estimate (6-8 months, 5 engineers) is project management metadata not a technical specification requirement.

answers.answer: The maximum acceptable latency for critical notifications is 500 milliseconds. This is measured end-to-end from ingestion API response to delivery confirmation webhook. The 99.9th percentile latency must be ≤ 500ms, the 99th percentile must be ≤ 350ms, and any single critical alert exceeding 750ms constitutes immediate test failure.
AES-256 encryption is required for patient data at rest, with 90-day key rotation via AWS KMS. This meets NIST standards and HIPAA §164.312(a)(2)(iv) addressable specifications.

The notification payload size limit is 4KB maximum. This is enforced to optimize for in-memory buffering without disk spillover and to keep mobile delivery snappy. Payloads exceeding this limit return HTTP 413 (Payload Too Large).

There are 4 notification priority levels: Critical (pager + push with immediate delivery), High (push within 30 seconds with expedited routing), Normal (push within 5 minutes with best-effort delivery), and Low (batched hourly summaries with 1 hour batched processing).
The beliefs provided do not specify data residency requirements for patient data. There is no information about geographic restrictions, regional requirements, or cross-border data routing policies.

Audit logs must be retained for a minimum of 7 years as mandated by HIPAA Section 164.530(j). The system uses an append-only log architecture with PostgreSQL partitioning by month, with estimated 500GB/year of audit data per region. Logs are immutable after creation.

The retry policy uses exponential backoff with 3 maximum retry attempts. The backoff sequence is 1s → 2s → 4s, capped at 30 seconds maximum. The system executes 3 attempts over 30 seconds max, running independently per channel. After 3 failed attempts, notifications are marked as permanently failed.

The system uses active-passive failover topology with a 30-second failure detection window and 60-second standby promotion time, resulting in a 90-second maximum client disruption window. Health checks run every 5 seconds via HTTP /health endpoints checking Kafka connectivity, downstream provider availability, and memory pressure.

No, the failover configuration is NOT consistent with the critical alert latency SLA. The 90-second maximum client disruption window (30s detection + 60s promotion) vastly exceeds the 500ms critical alert latency requirement. During a regional failover, critical alerts would experience delays up to 90 seconds, which is 180 times longer than the 500ms SLA. This represents a significant violation of the core product promise for patient safety.

The maximum total time before a failed notification is escalated to manual review is 24 hours. Calculation: The retry policy executes 3 attempts with exponential backoff (1s + 2s + 4s = 7 seconds total retry time). After retries are exhausted, the notification is marked as permanently failed. The dead letter queue has a 24-hour threshold, meaning notifications undelivered after 24 hours move to the DLQ for manual review. Therefore: 7 seconds (retries) + up to 24 hours (DLQ threshold) = approximately 24 hours total.

The WebSocket concurrent connection limit per relay node is exactly 10,000 connections. Dedicated relay nodes maintain these connections using epoll/kqueue for I/O multiplexing, with memory consumption <8GB per node at 10K connections and CPU utilization <70%.

The rate limit is 100 notifications per second per delivery channel (SMS, push, email, in-app) with burst capacity of 150 notifications per second. The burst capacity lasts for up to 10 seconds. This is implemented using a token bucket algorithm with a 10-second refill window at the provider adapter layer, with 500 tokens in the bucket (instead of 100) to provide the 10 seconds of burst capacity.

HashiCorp Vault is used as the certificate authority for service-to-service communication, with 24-hour certificate lifetimes. WebSocket connections carrying PHI must enforce TLS 1.2 minimum with forward secrecy cipher suites (ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384 or equivalent) per §164.312(e)(1) transmission security requirements.
Client API access uses JWT tokens with 15-minute expiration and automatic refresh token rotation. JWT tokens are verified at the API gateway with a 30-second clock skew tolerance.

Undelivered notifications after 24 hours move to the dead letter queue (DLQ) for manual review. DLQ entries persist indefinitely and are never auto-deleted. The DLQ uses time-series partitioned storage in DynamoDB with TTL disabled for DLQ partitions.

Complete lifecycle of a failed critical alert: (1) Initial delivery attempt fails; (2) Automatic retry begins with exponential backoff: 1st retry at 1 second, 2nd retry at 2 seconds, 3rd retry at 4 seconds (total 7 seconds of retry time); (3) After 3 failed attempts over maximum 30 seconds, the notification is marked as permanently failed; (4) Failed notification enters a waiting period; (5) At the 24-hour threshold from initial failure, the notification moves to the dead letter queue (DLQ) for manual review; (6) DLQ entries persist indefinitely and are never auto-deleted. Total maximum time to DLQ escalation: approximately 24 hours.

Full security architecture: (1) Encryption at rest: AES-256 for all stored patient data with 90-day key rotation via AWS KMS, meeting NIST standards and HIPAA §164.312(a)(2)(iv); (2) Service authentication: HashiCorp Vault as certificate authority with 24-hour certificate lifetimes; TLS 1.2 minimum with forward secrecy cipher suites (ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384 or equivalent) for WebSocket connections carrying PHI per §164.312(e)(1); (3) Client authentication: JWT tokens with 15-minute expiration and automatic refresh token rotation, verified at API gateway with 30-second clock skew tolerance; (4) Data residency: No specific requirements are defined in the beliefs provided.

Yes, the system can produce a 6-year-old notification audit log. The system maintains a 7-year audit retention period as mandated by HIPAA Section 164.530(j), which exceeds the 6-year request. Audit logs are stored using an append-only log architecture with PostgreSQL partitioning by month. Logs are immutable after creation and stored with estimated 500GB/year of audit data per region.
